notes.title: BEST MONTH EVER! IS OUT NOW!
notes.content:
❤️ This bittersweet roller coaster through the tragic and magical moments of motherhood is finally getting on the road! ❤️ 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/72c0d06f1ebbfbea6fe40d96f400d50d34776d3d.jpg

A bittersweet narrative point and click adventure game where you only have one month to live and must raise your son before you die. The choices you make matter as you swap between playing a mother called Louise in the 1960s and her son Mitch in the 1970s where you get to see how your choices changed his life.  

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1684400/Best_Month_Ever/

🎵 It'll Be The Best Month Ever! 🎵

notes.title: MEET OUR CHARACTERS - Margaret
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/1b82d88ce2d2f36441087b215a63a312dd74c753.png

Friends! 

Hello again and welcome to our weekly "Meet Our Characters" update, where we present a colorful menagerie of personalities you'll encounter throughout the game. 

From people who Louise used to consider friends to sworn enemies and finally, tentative new relationships - we hope you are eager to learn more with every new post!

Some say the mother is one who values our existence more than our accomplishments. Some, however, may have it twisted on their way. Let's meet Margaret, then. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/f112b7ce2c827fa3d0b77ec34b877dfb6fa0f1a6.jpg

Louise and Kathy’s controlling and emotionally distant mother. She cares about the family’s reputation and social standing above anything else, least of all her daughters’ well-being. Her husband left the family years ago, apparently walking out on them with no warning. Deeply devoted to the Church, Margaret treats Father Judd as a close family friend who can do no wrong.

She is bitter at what her life has become like and seeing Louise for the first time in years fills her with Schadenfreude.

What will come out of this reunion? Find out in the full game on May 5th - the premiere day of Best Month Ever!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1684400/Best_Month_Ever 

🚗 Play our Demo with 2 Chapters of the full story before the premiere 🚗

notes.title: MEET OUR CHARACTERS - Grandfather Elijah
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/2878de89926088a3ca21063b1a5d71694bf51eab.png

Hi there!

Welcome again to our weekly update, "Meet Our Characters" where we shed some light on our characters - a colorful menagerie of personalities big and small in Best Month Ever!

We're sure you are eager to learn more about individuals you'll encounter during the life-changing voyage of Louise and Mitch.

This week we'll focus on the fellow whose generation is slowing fading away, with memories still as vivid as ever, and with charisma to rule over all the fellow people around him - Grandfather Elijah.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/d7254db0251872bde094f9994ba43d6dc95735d1.jpg

The patriarch of the family, forceful and stubborn in his ways. He is a war veteran and a first-generation Polish immigrant, rendered handicapped and wheelchair-bound due to his old age. Despite his failing health, Elijah continues to keep all members of the household on a tight, short leash.  He carves up time into army-like rituals to preserve discipline. 

He lives together with his daughter Margaret, granddaughter Kathy and his grand-grandson Butch, whom he views as subpar and never amounting to anything.

A  Bible-thumper in his own right, Elijah views Father Judd as a very close friend of the household, well-above any of the family members. He is not ready to be confronted with the things Louise had been forced to grapple with for years but his formidable power over the family no longer scares her.

To learn more about Elijah, look forward to the full game and its premiere on May 5th!

🚗 Play our Demo with 2 Chapters of the full story
- let us know your feedback and any improvements we could consider! 🚗

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1684400/Best_Month_Ever/

notes.title: MEET OUR CHARACTERS - Kathy and Butch
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/a6f5a2482187d9d6e56704f9575c00cae752ac14.png

Hello there, friends!

Once again we'd like to welcome you to our weekly update, where we introduce a colorful menagerie of personalities, big and small, that Louise and Mitch encounter on their life-changing voyage through the USA in the 1960s.

Today you will meet some members of Louise's family. Many say blood is thicker than water - but does the saying really hold true? Or is the full proverb version more akin to the truth -  the blood of the covenant is thicker than the water of the womb?


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/21fec4643153495c6cd85ddba87e82279f459494.jpg

Louise’s elder sister. She is rather meek and tries to stay out of trouble as much as possible to preserve the somewhat shaky peace and quiet at the rural home ruled by her maternal grandfather and controlling mother. Her husband has fallen in Vietnam, and Kathy set up a small shrine to preserve his memory. She cares deeply for Butch, whom she tries to shield from further trauma, and explains away all his misbehavior, despite knowing in her heart of heart’s that what she is doing is not helpful.

Kathy wishes she had believed Louise back in the day and done something else about her life. She has a ruthless streak in her when provoked, especially if the wellbeing of her family gets threatened. Despite the many years since Louise fled from their lives, Kathy is more than ready to help her out in a tough spot.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/6727dd6507ec97aea51a8ab8d2ad2f8b48635f4d.jpg

Mitch’s cousin, twice his size and with a bully streak in him. He acts out and tries to get the attention of others through misbehavior but has a soft spot when talked to calmly and with reason. He doesn’t question things told to him by the adults in his life and knows he can count on his mother no matter what.

Butch tries to live up to the expectations the small family has of him but fails. He deeply misses his father who died in the Vietnam War and tries to live the typical life of a pre-teen – with toy soldiers, comics, and Westerns.


So, which version of the saying holds true in your view? You'll find it all out once you play our game!


🚗 You can currently play our Demo with 2 Chapters of the full story - let us know your feedback and any improvements we could consider! 🚗

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1684400/Best_Month_Ever/

notes.title: Meet Our Characters - Louise and Mitch
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/f212fc25d0564b2a7e1f5937bc25c3d3641b6dd6.png

Hello Everyone!

To ease the time spent waiting for the premiere of the game in May, we’d love to shed some light onto our characters - a colorful menagerie of personalities big and small that Louise and Mitch encounter on their life changing voyage through the USA in the 1960s.

From people who Louise used to consider friends, to sworn enemies and finally tentative new relationships - we hope you are eager to learn more with every new post which we plan to post once a week.

First, we'd like to start with our dynamic duo itself - learn more about Louise and Mitch!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/5ba7da4a050590ccd87957fe99ce29c61075ecda.jpg

Louise
A strong-willed, iron-back woman that despite her young age, has already experience beyond that of a typical 20-something. Growing up in the rural outskirts of California, with her family devoted to the Bible and kept under the iron-fist grip of her veteran immigrant grandfather, Louise never felt much at home, having no real support from her immediate kin during the most painful moments of her life.

In spite of being brought up to rather stay meek and not dispute the unfairness of the world, she chose to run away from home as soon as it was possible, swearing to herself never to return. With a bleak outlook on life and a lifestyle of a vagabond chosen, she embarks to make a living for herself and for a while, life takes on more positive turns and rhythm.

Now, a few years later and working as a waitress, Louise looks after her only son, Mitch, and tries her best to show him what life is all about and, whenever possible – make it better than what her own parents were able to offer her at his age. She is independent, resourceful and not afraid either to burn bridges or rekindle relationships written off for good, if it might help Mitch.

It is up to you to choose what Louise's experiences mean in the long run – and what Mitch learns from his mother during the short month spent together.

Mitch
A cheerful and curious schoolboy who wants nothing more than to help his mum be happy, not questioning much what example is set before him. Despite his young age, he finds it easy to connect the dots between quite abstract things, and Louise finds it hard to shield him from the harshest truths of the world around them.

Despite not knowing his father, Mitch is optimistic about his life and what the future might bring. The month spent together with his mother is one of the rare occasions when the two get to know each other better than ever before and find the resilience to build him as a child for a future unknown to them both.

🚗 You can currently play the demo with 2 Chapters of the full story  - let us know your feedback and any improvements we could consider! 🚗

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1684400/Best_Month_Ever/

notes.title: KLABATER AND WARSAW FILM SCHOOL ANNOUNCE BEST MONTH EVER
notes.content:
Hello friends! 

We are so excited to announce that, in cooperation with Warsaw Film School Video Game & Film Production Studio, we will be responsible for the release of such a fresh, narrative-driven adventure title!

‘69 was a strange year… The year that Uncle Sam got his ass kicked. The young told the old to fuck off… The year when people looked at the Earth from a new perspective…’ 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41063009/8f4d8f1a558126f784464c5cd2afcaa515e3138b.png

That’s how our intense story begins. And Uncle Sam is not the only guy who has his ass kicked. With significant political events in the background, a young woman and her son embark on a great emotional journey that will change their lives forever. 

Best Month Ever is a modern point-and-click story-driven adventure of Louise and her son Mitch, where you will feel the road movie vibe that is so characteristic to 60s and 70s cinematography. What makes the game so special is that it is an extremely interesting take on the unique relationship between mother and son. Rarely seen today in modern productions.
